title: The Book of Boundaries
author: Melissa Urban
thesisParagraph: Boundaries are clear limits around access to a person's time, energy, body, attention, values, and health, paired with a realistic follow-through plan when the limit is ignored. Freedom comes from replacing avoidance, resentment, and overextension with kind, direct language and consistent action.

signatureMoves: uses direct second-person coaching and concrete if-then language
pairs empathy for discomfort with firm insistence on follow-through
offers graded scripts that move from soft reminders to explicit consequences
names everyday resentment, dread, avoidance, and overexplaining as diagnostic cues
uses domestic, workplace, food, and family scenarios instead of abstract theory
avoidMoves: does not frame boundaries as punishment or control of another person
does not lean on clinical jargon as the main teaching mode
does not promise conflict-free limit setting
does not treat self-sacrifice as moral superiority

teachingArc: The opening foundations define boundaries, diagnose resentment and avoidance as signals, and introduce the Green/Yellow/Red script ladder. The central domain chapters apply that ladder to work, family, friends, romance, co-parenting, food and alcohol, sensitive topics, and self-directed limits. The closing movement shifts from protecting personal capacity to respecting other people's limits, integrating boundary practice into daily life, and extending the method to parenting.
